Your Store Owner Handbook

Run your Shopify store with confidence, not anxiety.

A plain‑English walkthrough of everything you actually need: the dashboard, products, orders, payments, shipping, and the simple rhythm of daily and weekly tasks. No code. No jargon. Just the parts that matter.

7 Short Modules Curated Videos Daily & Weekly SOPs
Start Here · Read This First

Your store is custom on the outside. Standard Shopify on the inside.

This is the single most important thing to understand before anything else, and it's the thing that will quietly answer most of the worries you might have about your store.

Your storefront — the part your customers see when they visit your website — was custom built for you. It's faster and more polished than a typical Shopify theme. But behind the scenes, your store runs on Shopify itself, the same platform that powers more than a million online businesses worldwide.

That means everything that matters is handled by tools that have been tested, refined, and trusted for years:

1Products live in Shopify
2Orders process through Shopify
3Payments run through Shopify
4Inventory tracks in Shopify
5Customer data sits in Shopify

Think of it this way: Shopify is the engine. Your custom site is the bodywork. Everything safe, proven, and reliable about Shopify is still doing the heavy lifting underneath — you just got a much nicer car wrapped around it.

So when you log into your Shopify admin (Module 1 below), you're working with the same tool every other Shopify merchant uses. Same buttons. Same flows. Same support. Every video in this handbook was made for regular Shopify users — and it applies directly to your store.

Module 01

Your Shopify Dashboard

The dashboard (Shopify calls it the "admin") is your command center. Once you know your way around the left‑hand sidebar, you can run the entire store from here.

Start by getting comfortable with where things live. You don't need to click into every option on day one — just know that the sections you'll use most are Orders, Products, and Customers, all near the top of the sidebar.

Shopify Admin Essentials · Official Shopify Academy Watch

What to remember

  • The sidebar on the left is how you navigate — Home, Orders, Products, Customers, Analytics, Marketing, Discounts.
  • Click the gear icon (Settings, bottom‑left) for store‑wide settings: shipping, taxes, payments, notifications.
  • The top search bar finds orders, products, and customers fast — use it instead of scrolling.
  • The Shopify mobile app gives you the same dashboard on your phone. Useful for checking orders on the go.
Module 02

Managing Products

Adding products is the most frequent task you'll do. Once you've done it three or four times, it becomes muscle memory.

For each product, you'll fill in a title, description, photos, price, and inventory count. Shopify automatically makes the product show up on your storefront once you save it as Active. If you want to hide a product, switch it to Draft — it stays in your system, just not visible to customers.

How to Add a Product · Official Shopify Help Center walkthrough Watch

Product checklist

  • Title — clear and descriptive (e.g. "Brushed Cotton Throw — Forest Green").
  • Description — what it is, who it's for, why it's good. A few short paragraphs is plenty.
  • Photos — at least 3. The first photo is the one customers see in the catalog.
  • Price — required. "Compare at" price shows a strikethrough sale price if you want one.
  • Inventory — turn on "Track quantity" if you have a fixed stock; Shopify will warn you when it runs low.
  • Status — Active (visible) or Draft (hidden). Set to Active when ready.
Module 03

Orders & Checkout

This is usually the most worrying part for new store owners — and the part Shopify handles best. Here's what actually happens when a customer buys something.

A customer adds a product to their cart, clicks checkout, fills in their address, and pays. Shopify takes the payment, sends them a confirmation email, and creates an order in your dashboard. You don't have to do anything for the order to appear — it just shows up under the Orders tab, ready for you to fulfill.

Most stores get a notification too (email or mobile push) the moment an order comes in. We'll cover those notifications in Module 6.

How To Fulfill Orders On Shopify · Step-by-step for beginners (2025) Watch

The order flow in plain English

  • Customer pays → order appears in your Orders tab with status "Unfulfilled".
  • You pack the item and print the shipping label (Module 5 covers this).
  • You click "Mark as Fulfilled" in Shopify — this triggers an automatic shipping email to the customer.
  • Order status updates to "Fulfilled" and you're done.
Module 04

Getting Paid — Shopify Payments

Shopify Payments is the built‑in payment processor. It accepts credit cards, debit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Shop Pay. The money goes from the customer's card to your bank account on a regular schedule — usually a few business days.

You'll connect your business bank account once during setup. After that, Shopify handles every transaction automatically. You can see every payment, fee, and payout under Settings → Payments and Finances → Payouts.

Setting Up Payments · Official Shopify Academy Watch

What to know about payments

  • Transaction fees — Shopify Payments charges a small percentage per sale (typically 2.4–2.9% + 30¢). This is normal and built into your price.
  • Payouts — money lands in your bank account on a rolling schedule (you can see exactly when under "Payouts").
  • Refunds — issued in two clicks from inside the order. The customer gets their money back to the same card.
  • Chargebacks — rare, but Shopify will email you if one happens. Don't panic; there's a simple process to respond.
  • If you ever want to also accept PayPal or another method, that gets added under Settings → Payments.
Module 05

Shipping & Fulfillment

Once an order comes in, you ship it. Shopify can buy and print shipping labels for you (USPS, UPS, DHL) at discounted rates — no need to drive to the post office for label paperwork.

You'll set your shipping rates once under Settings → Shipping and Delivery. Most stores use a flat rate or weight‑based rate per package. Once that's done, every customer sees the right shipping cost automatically at checkout.

How to Set Up Shopify Shipping · Official Shopify Help Center Watch

Shipping in three steps

  • Buy the label directly from inside the order in Shopify.
  • Print it on a regular printer or thermal label printer, and tape it to the package.
  • Click "Mark as fulfilled" — Shopify auto‑emails the tracking number to the customer.
Module 06

Customer Notifications

Shopify automatically sends professional, branded emails to customers at every step of the order. You don't have to write them or send them — they just happen.

Order confirmation, shipping confirmation, delivery confirmation, refund notice — all of it is automated. You can customize the wording or branding under Settings → Notifications if you ever want to, but the defaults are perfectly fine to start.

Notifications worth knowing

  • Order confirmation — sent the moment a customer pays.
  • Shipping confirmation — sent when you click "Mark as fulfilled" (includes tracking).
  • Out for delivery / delivered — sent automatically by the carrier integration.
  • Refund notification — sent when you issue a refund.
  • You will also receive an email (and mobile push, if you have the Shopify app) for every new order.
Module 07

Abandoned Cart Recovery · for later

An "abandoned cart" is when a customer adds something to their cart, starts checkout, then leaves before paying. About 70% of all carts get abandoned everywhere — it's normal. Shopify can automatically email those customers a gentle reminder.

This isn't something to set up on day one. Get comfortable with the basics first. But when you're ready (a few weeks in), this single feature can recover meaningful revenue with almost no effort.

Shopify Abandoned Cart — Free Built-in Setup · Marketing Automations walkthrough Watch

Bookmark for later

  • Found under Marketing → Automations in your Shopify admin.
  • Shopify provides a free built‑in abandoned cart email template — turn it on and it's running.
  • A typical setup: one reminder email 1 hour after abandonment, a second 24 hours later.
  • Expect to recover roughly 5–15% of abandoned carts once the automation is on.
Module 08

Your Daily & Weekly Rhythm

The whole platform can feel overwhelming until you settle into a simple routine. These two short checklists are the only thing you really need to keep the store healthy.

Daily — 10 to 15 minutes

Every Morning

  1. Open Shopify and check the Orders tab for anything new.
  2. Fulfill any unfulfilled orders — print labels, pack, ship.
  3. Reply to any new customer emails or messages.
  4. Glance at Home for today's sales and visitor count.
  5. Spot‑check inventory on best‑sellers (low‑stock warnings appear automatically).
Weekly — 30 to 45 minutes

Once a Week

  1. Review the Analytics tab — what sold, what didn't.
  2. Add any new products or update existing ones.
  3. Restock items running low (or mark them sold out).
  4. Check Finances → Payouts to confirm money is landing correctly.
  5. Review any abandoned checkouts and take note of patterns.

You don't need to memorize any of this.

You just need to know where it lives. Bookmark this handbook, work through one module at a time, and let the videos do the heavy lifting. Within a couple of weeks, the Shopify admin will feel as familiar as your email inbox — and your store will quietly run itself in the background while you focus on the customers in front of you.
